purpose: Track B2.0. Synthetic multi-event recordings where one fixed-size latent must trade off evidence and different questions about the same recording need different evidence. This run only checks the full-audio positive control and whether audio-only bottlenecks lose accuracy as the number of events grows.

source.dataset: ESC-50 at the commit pinned in prepare.py
source.development_half: Sort fold 2 src_file IDs, shuffle with split_seed, assign the first half to development and the rest to confirmation. Confirmation stimuli are not generated or evaluated in this run.
source.excluded_folds: 3, 4 and 5 were used by track A

stimuli.event_window: The 1.5 s window of the source clip with the highest mean energy, 50 ms hop, 10 ms fades, normalized to equal RMS.
stimuli.placement: Choose N of the 6 equal slots at random; jitter the event start uniformly within the slot.
stimuli.peak_rule: Scale an event down only if its own peak exceeds peak_limit. Events never overlap, so the limit is applied per event and does not change the other events in the recording.

questions.development: Per recording one yes question about a random present category and one no question about a random absent category. Each is the other's wrong-stem donor.
questions.train: Per recording min(N, 3) yes questions and the same number of no questions.
questions.negative_rule: The absent category must not share a confusion group with any present category.

evaluation.models: Full audio, text only, and the existing Clotho-trained audio-only compressors runs/guidance/k{1,4,16}-s{17,18,19}-audio as a preview. The B2 grid will retrain on the synthetic train split.
evaluation.score: yes logit minus no logit at the first answer token, per option order

gates.bottleneck_pressure: Audio-only K=1 accuracy (mean of orders and seeds) at N=6 at least 10 points below N=1. Checked on the preview here and again on the synthetic-trained models.

evaluation.interval: Bootstrap over recordings, seed 17, 10000 replicates. Source clips recur across recordings, so intervals are approximate.
